B's one-color and reversed marks are just solid hexagons: the M and the river wave disappear, so the logo fails on caps, vinyl and burned frames. That outweighs its stronger Maumee-river idea. A's stacked hive-box mark is a simple solid shape that reads the same at 16 and 32 px and holds up in one ink and reversed. Both spell the name exactly and invent nothing, and both marks are just the initials O and R, so neither has a real idea. B wins on the brief's second test: its heavy, simple O and R stay the same clear shape at 32 and 16 px and in one color, while A's thin serif OR blurs inside the circle at 16 px, and its fine serifs and light subline are risky for cut vinyl. A's lockup is better balanced and its round mark suits the circle avatar. B's mark is too small next to the wordmark and its R counter nearly closes up, so the margin is slight.

Both spell the name correctly and add nothing to it. A's heavy geometric O and R stay the same clear shape at 32 and 16 px and are solid enough to cut in white vinyl. B's thin serif 'OR' blurs inside its circle at 16 px, and its light 'Certified Public Accountants' line in Cormorant would be fragile on the glass door. Neither idea comes from the client's own subject, since both are initial monograms, but A's bold, custom-looking letterforms are more distinctive than B's default serif in a circle, which any competitor could use as-is.

Both spell the name correctly and invent nothing. A falls apart in one color: the otter's head merges into the solid circle so only a muzzle and thin whiskers are left, and the thin whiskers and wave line turn to mush at 16 px. Neither guide invents anything: both stick to the brief's facts. B is the more usable handoff. It has logo clear-space and do-not-crop rules, a full contrast table, named fonts (Fraunces and Work Sans) with a size scale, voice examples set out as Say/Not pairs taken from real brief details, and imagery Do/Don't lists specific enough to judge a photo against. B loses some ground for small slips: the footer lists logo.svg twice, Bank Plaster and Warm Chalk share the same hex, and the ochre logo tile is too small to read.
